question: How does Theme.of(context) know which widgets to rebuild when the theme changes?
shortAnswer: Theme is an InheritedWidget; of(context) registers a dependency so dependents rebuild when updateShouldNotify is true.
strongAnswer: InheritedWidget lookup via dependOnInheritedWidgetOfExactType registers the Element as dependent. When the inherited widget updates and updateShouldNotify returns true, Flutter marks dependents dirty. That is why Theme/MediaQuery/Localizations rebuild consumers without manual listeners.
advancedAnswer: Explain Provider/Riverpod as ergonomic layers over similar dependency mechanisms and rebuild scoping.
followUps: How would you avoid rebuilding a huge subtree on a chatty inherited value?
What is the difference between dependOn vs getElementForInheritedWidget?
commonWrongAnswer: Flutter magically rebuilds the whole app on any theme change with no dependency tracking.
productionRelevance: Dark mode and brand theme toggles must be scoped; otherwise entire trees rebuild and lists jank.
